decision: routed to figure-it-out instead of Feature
why: greenfield app with three parts (iOS app, Mac bridge, cloud dispatch) is a multi-part change

decision: probed Agent SDK against the installed claude CLI before designing
why: riskiest unknown was whether a Mac bridge could run tasks on the user's own login and route permission prompts to the phone
result: VERIFIED: canUseTool fired for Bash, file written, session_id returned

decision: used Grok Bot (xAI, Aug 2026) as the UX reference only
why: it is a chat-with-bots app with approval cards and push alerts and has no public pairing protocol to copy

decision: cloud tasks run through claude --cloud on the Mac under a pseudo-terminal
why: '--cloud refuses --print for new sessions, but in a pty it prints the session id and exits; this keeps the user's subscription login and real Claude Code cloud sessions

decision: cloud tasks show no live stream, only created, follow-up queued, open in Claude
why: '--cloud <id> rejects stream-json, and Managed Agents would need an API key and a separate product
evidence: CLI error: --cloud <session_id> does not support --output-format stream-json
result: open: Managed Agents backend is a follow-up

decision: skipped arena for the protocol shape
why: greenfield and both ends are ours, so the shape is a cheap two-way door; one designed union plus a shared fixture covers it

decision: split the build into two parallel delegates, bridge/ and ios/, after committing the protocol
why: the two parts touch disjoint folders and share only the protocol, which is now fixed and read-only for both

decision: accepted the bridge delegate's work after rerunning its tests myself
why: a delegate's report is not proof
evidence: bun test: 51 pass 0 fail; delegate e2e: E2E PASS against haiku

decision: drove the real app against the real bridge in the simulator: pair by deep link, create a Mac task, approve Write and Bash, read the reply
why: the delegates only tested each half alone
evidence: /tmp/claude-501/s6.png s7.png s8.png; hello.py contains print("hello from ClaudioBot")

decision: found four polish bugs while driving the app
why: absolute /private/var paths in summaries, centered code in approval cards, Bash approval repeats the command, smart quotes in prompts

decision: created a cloud task on nx-starter from the app, then sent a follow-up
why: proves the cloud path through the real UI, not just the parser tests

decision: found two cloud UX gaps: idle cloud task reads Done, and the form shows model and permission pickers the cloud path ignores
why: a dispatched cloud task is still working remotely, and showing controls that do nothing misleads

decision: rebuilt the app with all fixes and reopened it against the live bridge
why: check the fixes on the real paired app, not only demo data
evidence: /tmp/claude-501/s14.png: cloud task shows In cloud, Mac task shows Done

decision: studied the user's live Grok Bot on Mac and iPhone with computer use
why: user said the task-proxy design duplicates the Claude iOS app and asked for Grok Bot's actual behaviour

decision: replace tasks with persistent bots that own a conversation, memory, routines, a library and the agents they start
why: Grok Bot's unit is a long-lived bot with one job, not a coding session; Redesign from First Principles

decision: bot questions are a non-blocking ask tool whose answer arrives as a new message
why: Grok cards stay open for days and survive restarts; a blocking canUseTool promise would not
evidence: mac-chat-question-card.jpg shows a card answered hours later

decision: the Computer tab becomes an Agents tab
why: Claudio bots have no VM of their own; showing a fake screen would mislead, and the agents a bot started are the real work surface; Experience First

decision: cloud agents are fire-and-follow with a link
why: claude --cloud gives no completion signal to another program (verified last run); local agents report back on every turn
evidence: decisions.tsv rows from the first run

decision: did not permanently delete the test bot New Bot created during observation
why: permanent deletion stays with the user
evidence: Grok delete dialog says it cannot be undone

decision: bridge v2 ships permissionMode auto for bots and mac agents
why: auto was accepted by claude 2.1.301 with no denials for MCP tools and Write
evidence: delegate probe; e2e (c) agent created and committed hello.txt

decision: re-ran bridge tests and tsc myself
why: own every delegate's work

decision: relayed three bridge facts to the iOS builder (library paths, pushed agent upserts, re-open to clear unread)
why: they extend the protocol's meaning without changing its shape

decision: live app plus real bridge on the simulator, Haiku, temp home
why: Prove It Works on the real artifact
evidence: Claudio Bot greeted; mac agent committed CONTRIBUTING.md (ea71c20) and reported back; New Bot onboarding card answered and the bot renamed itself Builder; routine created, shown Weekdays at 9:00 AM, paused and resumed through the app; avatar change round-tripped; exchange view showed the agent thread

decision: split bubbles at paragraphs, drop text after ask in the same turn, keep internals out of chat
why: live run showed walls of text, narration after the card and USER.md mentions; Grok does none of these
evidence: simulator screenshots of Claudio Bot and New Bot

decision: bubble split and voice fixes checked live
why: own the delegate's work
evidence: bun test 92 pass; tsc clean; live reply arrived as three bubbles (summary, numbered list, offer)

decision: chat must follow new messages and inset for the composer
why: live run: replies landed hidden behind the composer

decision: chat auto-scroll fix checked
why: own the delegate's work
evidence: live-after-reply.png: newest reply visible above the composer; xcodebuild test 38 pass
